question: Why does the Agents framework capture video frames at a configurable interval rather than sending every frame to the LLM?
options: The I2S bus cannot transmit video frames faster than the configured interval
Sending every frame would be prohibitively expensive in tokens and too slow for real-time conversation
WebRTC video Tracks only deliver frames at the capture interval rate
Multimodal LLMs can only process one image per API call
explanation: A single 1024x768 frame costs 750-1000 tokens. Sending frames at 30fps would consume millions of tokens per minute and add seconds of latency to every LLM call. Strategic capture at 1-5 second intervals balances visual awareness with cost and speed.

question: What is the key difference between continuous observation and on-demand analysis patterns for vision agents?
options: Continuous observation requires a separate vision model from the conversation LLM
On-demand analysis uses higher resolution frames than continuous observation
Continuous observation captures at shorter intervals to notice changes proactively, while on-demand waits for the user to ask before analyzing the current frame
Continuous observation uses camera Tracks while on-demand uses screen share Tracks
explanation: Continuous observation (like monitoring a lab experiment) uses short capture intervals so the agent can proactively notice and report changes. On-demand analysis (like reading a textbook page) provides high-quality analysis of a specific moment only when the user asks, saving tokens during passive periods.

question: How should a vision agent handle cases where it cannot clearly read text from a camera image?
options: Acknowledge the limitation honestly and ask the user to adjust lighting, distance, or focus
Use a fallback OCR library to extract the text automatically
Switch to a higher-resolution capture mode automatically
Make its best guess based on partial character recognition
explanation: LLMs can hallucinate text that is not actually in the image, especially when it is ambiguous. A careful vision agent should express confidence levels, quote text exactly, and ask the user to improve conditions rather than guessing and potentially providing incorrect information.
